title: Test Generation Agent
description: Analyze coverage gaps and generate comprehensive test suites for your code.

unit.placeholder: Select a file for unit test generation

userStory.label: User Story
userStory.placeholder: Describe the user story or scenario...

description.label: What should this code do?
description.placeholder: Describe the behaviour to implement. Example: a function that calculates the total price of a cart including taxes and discounts, handling empty carts and negative quantities.

filePicker.selectFile: Browse and select a source file...

errors.noFile: Please select a file to analyze
errors.generic: An error occurred during test generation

auth.title: The AI provider rejected your credentials
auth.hint: Open Settings → Providers and re-authenticate the active provider. If you sign in with a Claude subscription, your session may simply have expired.

rate_limit.title: Rate limit reached
rate_limit.hint: The provider is throttling requests. Wait a moment and try again, or switch to another account or provider in Settings.

quota.title: No credit left on this account
quota.hint: The provider accepted the request but refused to bill it. Check your plan or billing status, then try again.

network.title: The provider could not be reached
network.hint: Check your internet connection, and any VPN or corporate proxy between you and the provider.

timeout.title: The provider took too long to answer
timeout.hint: Large source files make the model slower. Try again, or generate tests for a smaller file.

provider_unavailable.title: The provider could not be started
provider_unavailable.hint: The CLI or Python dependency behind the selected provider is missing or not on PATH. Check Settings → Providers and your local installation.

empty_response.title: The provider returned nothing
empty_response.hint: The request was accepted but produced no text. This usually means the model refused the prompt or the response was cut short — try again, or pick another model in Settings.

file_not_found.title: The source file could not be read
file_not_found.hint: Check that the file still exists, is not empty, and is UTF-8 text rather than a binary.

write_failed.title: The test file could not be written
write_failed.hint: The tests were generated but not saved. Check the folder's permissions and free disk space, then copy the code above before retrying.

parse_failed.title: The provider's answer could not be read
parse_failed.hint: The model replied with something other than the expected JSON. Trying again usually resolves it; a more capable model resolves it more reliably.

invalid_input.title: Something is missing from the request
invalid_input.hint: Fill in the highlighted field and start the generation again.

backend_missing.title: The WorkPilot AI backend was not found
backend_missing.hint: The Python backend that runs the generator is missing from this installation. Reinstall the app, or run it from the repository so apps/backend is present.

runner_crashed.title: The generator stopped unexpectedly
runner_crashed.hint: The generator process died before it could report anything. The technical details below carry the reason it printed on the way out.

no_output.title: The generator finished without producing tests
no_output.hint: The process ran to completion but wrote nothing. Check that the source file is readable and that your provider is authenticated in Settings.

unknown.title: Test generation failed
unknown.hint: Open the technical details below for the raw error. Trying again is safe — nothing has been written to your project.

destination.title: Where should these tests go?
destination.noTestsDir: This project keeps its sources in {{sourceRoot}} but has no test directory beside it. Choose where to write the generated tests — the directory is created if it does not exist.
destination.noSourceRoot: No source or test directory could be found in this project. Choose where to write the generated tests — the directory is created if it does not exist.

libraries.title: Test libraries
libraries.description: What the generated tests are written against. Pre-filled from the packages this project already references.
libraries.missingWarning_one: {{count}} package is not referenced yet ({{packages}}). The generated tests will not compile until it is added.
libraries.missingWarning_other: {{count}} packages are not referenced yet ({{packages}}). The generated tests will not compile until they are added.
libraries.installFailed: Some packages could not be added.

target.storyPlaceholder: As a buyer, I can pay my cart by card and I get a confirmation email. A declined payment shows a clear message.
target.targetHint: the file, route or screen under test
target.noLibraries: No library to pick for this language: the tests follow the framework detected in the project.

analyze.title: What lacks tests
analyze.body: The agent reads the file and your existing tests, then ranks every uncovered function by priority. Nothing is written to the project.

unit.title: A unit test file
unit.body: The file is written in your project's framework and libraries, then placed where your tests already live.

e2e.title: End-to-end tests
e2e.body: Each user story criterion becomes a Given / When / Then scenario, on the project's E2E tool (Playwright, Cypress, Capybara, Dusk, integration_test…).

tdd.title: Tests first
tdd.body: Describe what the code must do: the agent writes tests that fail until the implementation exists (red phase).

pipeline.legend: Click a step to see its result on the right.

analyze: The detected framework tells the model what a test already is here.
The code and your tests go to the model, nothing else.
Each untested function is ranked: business logic first.
unit: The project's framework and libraries set the idiom of the tests.
The source code and your existing tests go to the model.
The file is placed by the project's layout, never at the root.
e2e: The project's language picks the E2E tool: Playwright, Cypress, Dusk…
Each criterion becomes a Given / When / Then scenario.
The suite goes to the project's e2e folder.
tdd: The chosen language decides the framework, read from the project.
The model writes the tests, never the implementation.
The tests fail until the code exists.

empty.codeTitle: The file will be written here, live

code.unit: Pick a file and run the generation: the code arrives line by line.
code.e2e: Describe the scenario and its target, then run the generation.
code.tdd: Describe the expected behaviour, then run the generation.

empty.tests: The tests of the generated file show here, with what each one checks.
empty.gaps: Pick a file and run the analysis: functions without tests show here, most important first.

inspector.analyzing: The model compares the code with your existing tests.
inspector.noGapsBody: Every function in this file already has tests.

facts.destinationLater: decided at run time, from the project's layout

inspector.stackNote: Language, framework and libraries are read from the project's manifests (csproj, package.json, pyproject, go.mod, Cargo.toml, composer.json, Gemfile, pubspec.yaml, Package.swift, Gradle, Maven, CMake): nothing to configure.

composer.ready: Ready. Ctrl + Enter runs the agent.

running.analyze: The agent is analyzing the file…
running.unit: The agent is writing the tests…
running.e2e: The agent is writing the scenarios…
running.tdd: The agent is writing the red tests…

missing.e2e: Describe the user story and its target.
missing.tdd: Describe what the code must do.
